title: Did Smiths Lake Once Have Fruit Plantations? 1901
description:
Did Smiths Lake Once Have Fruit Plantations?
We're searching for a piece of our local history that hasn't yet made it into the written record.
Community memory suggests there may have been banana and/or passionfruit cultivation in the Smiths Lake area — possibly on farms run by some of our earliest settler families. But so far, we haven't been able to confirm it from historical documents or archives.

title: Naming of Pacific Palms (1959)
description:
The Name 'Pacific Palms' was Invented in 1959 - The Story
The name 'Pacific Palms' — now the official address for Blueys Beach, Boomerang Beach, and the broader area — is not a historical geographical name of any antiquity.  It was deliberately coined by a local progress association in 1959, specifically to make the area sound more appealing to Sydney real estate buyers.  The name was chosen as part of Degotardi's broader marketing campaign — a deliberate rebranding of what had simply been known as the Smiths Lake district.

title: Worimi Heritage
description:
The Worimi People and Smiths Lake — A Story Being Developed.  
Smiths Lake sits at the heart of Worimi country.  For thousands of years before European arrival, this remarkable combination of coastal lagoon, ocean access, abundant fish, and surrounding forest made it one of the most productive and significant places in the Worimi world.
This is a story we are committed to telling well — and that means telling it in Worimi voices, with Worimi guidance.
We are currently working to develop this history in partnership with the Forster Local Aboriginal Land Council, and we look forward to sharing it here as that conversation grows.
We acknowledge the Worimi people as the traditional custodians of the land on which Smiths Lake Village is located, and pay our respects to Elders past, present and emerging.
